stories.title: Microsoft 365 services return after global outage
stories.summary: Microsoft 365 services are back online following a 24-hour outage that impacted businesses and governments in over 70 countries. The disruption began Thursday afternoon and affected users globally. Microsoft has not yet provided a full explanation for the cause of the service failure.

stories.title: Gaming industry report highlights layoffs and AI
stories.summary: A GDC survey of industry workers identifies layoffs and generative AI as the primary concerns for game developers in 2026. The report, which includes data from 900 laid-off workers, describes a difficult environment for the sector. The industry continues to release games while sentiment remains low.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude for Manufacturing
stories.summary: Anthropic has released a plugin for manufacturing systems featuring 17 skills across operations, supply chain, and design. It supports connectors for Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365, and Oracle NetSuite. The company says the tool is built so a human can approve work before it reaches the customer.

stories.title: Tech layoffs continue through 2026
stories.summary: Tech companies cut nearly 110,000 jobs by mid-May, approaching the 125,000 total cuts seen in 2025. While some firms cite AI investment as a driver, others point to structural issues or product failures. A job in the industry is no longer the steady paycheck it once was.

stories.title: FAA expands AI air traffic tool
stories.summary: The FAA has expanded an AI tool to manage national airspace congestion. The agency claims the $875 million system saved 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel per flight in initial tests. The labor union representing air traffic controllers says it was not involved in the system's design.

stories.title: Canadian publishers proceed with OpenAI lawsuit
stories.summary: The Ontario Court of Appeal has dismissed an appeal by OpenAI, allowing a copyright lawsuit from a coalition of Canadian publishers to proceed. The group, which includes The Globe and Mail and CBC, alleges the company uses their content to train ChatGPT without permission.

stories.title: OpenAI faces patent infringement claims
stories.summary: A Texas technology company has sued OpenAI for allegedly infringing on patents related to artificial intelligence attention mechanisms. The same company filed a similar lawsuit against Anthropic on the same day. The full details of the legal filing are available to Law360 subscribers.

stories.title: Chinese AI labs reportedly using Nvidia chips
stories.summary: A forensic report suggests Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia Blackwell chips despite US export controls. The report claims to have identified the chip's fingerprint in models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. Nvidia has not commented on the findings.

stories.title: White House task force considers AI liability relief
stories.summary: A White House task force has suggested that companies should receive liability relief for cyberattacks involving artificial intelligence. The proposal aims to address security concerns as AI integration increases. Further details on the task force recommendations are available to Cybersecurity Dive subscribers.

stories.title: Cato Institute weighs in on AI policy
stories.summary: The Cato Institute suggests the new Congress has a unique opportunity to shape AI policy. The organization advocates for a sensible approach to regulation. The full analysis regarding the legislative outlook is available to Cato Institute subscribers.

stories.title: OpenAI board member discusses AI risks
stories.summary: An OpenAI board member has suggested that AI accidents could pose a fatal risk to individuals. The comments were made during a public discussion on the future of the technology. The full report on the board member's prediction is available to Fast Company subscribers.

stories.title: Irish premier calls for AI regulation
stories.summary: Irish premier Micheál Martin stated that AI should be designed for the benefit rather than the ruination of mankind. During a summit in Dublin, Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton urged global leaders to implement strict governance and regulation to manage the potential risks of the technology.

stories.title: Mistral CEO calls for faster European AI investment
stories.summary: Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch told EU leaders that Europe must act with speed and bolder financing to remain competitive in the AI race. He urged the bloc to increase its support for the sector immediately to avoid falling behind global rivals.

stories.title: Anthropic warns of AI safety score limitations
stories.summary: Anthropic has cautioned that AI safety scores can be misleading, noting that building effective metrics is difficult. The company suggests that current evaluation methods may not fully capture the risks of the technology. The full warning is available to Benzinga subscribers.

stories.title: OpenAI board member warns of potential AI takeover
stories.summary: Paul Cristiano, a board member of the OpenAI Foundation, warned that a societal takeover by AI could occur within 6 to 12 months if development continues on its fastest trajectory. He described this outcome as having a near coin-flip probability.

stories.title: Nasdaq considers delisting Subgen AI
stories.summary: Nasdaq Stockholm is considering a motion to delist Subgen AI from the First North Growth Market. The exchange alleges the company breached disclosure obligations and EU market abuse regulations. Subgen AI has been given an opportunity to respond to the claims.
